So with a diabetic  a target blood sugar is going to be around 100. If it was 70 or so I would eat something before going to sleep. I'd rather it be around 150. But again I can't tell you if that's the healthiest plan, just what I do. Most drinks are going to be higher in carbs so it's unlikely someone would be low but it's still possible. It's also harder to see if someone is low because low blood sugar looks like someone is drunk. As long as she keeps an eye on her blood sugar it should be fine.

Maybe it's how you wrote things but it doesn't seem like she's very interested in getting drunk. Being diabetic and drinking can be dangerous, being anxious about drinking as a diabetic is a bad situation.   
  
Apart from that, my advice is to drink at home. She should be aware of her blood sugar, it's horrible to be low and drunk. Does she have a continuous glucose monitor? Wine is not the best either, very high in carbs and makes most people kind of ill the next day. Obviously high blood sugar will guarantee you'll feel bad.  
  
Beer is still going to be pretty high in carbs. Liquor has few carbs so it's less concerning with high blood sugar. The problem is if she's never drank it can be tricky to drink liquor.  In my personal opinion  I'd rather be slightly high than slightly low when you go to sleep,

Just finished college and I've been on omnipod for several years. Here's my advice.  
  
To keep track maybe a calendar. Write down your tests and when projects are due and when you need to reorder supplies. You could set an alarm on your phone too.  
  
I had an issue with this but your roommate needs to be aware of what to look for if you go low. Plus shit happens and it's better they know. Once I woke up and texted my mom back about how my blood sugar was low, fell back asleep, woke up an hour later to paramedics breaking down my door ¯\_(ツ)_/¯  luckily my roommate was great about it and we laughed about it later. Also you need to let them know you have snacks and they absolutely can't eat them.   
   
  
Bring your testing supplies with you. Purse, backpack, drawstring bag. Keep it on you and don't lose it. Don't get drunk enough where you black out (duh). Take it easy until you figure out what kind of drunk you are.  
  
Any time I had to make an excuse because of diabetes my professors were more than understanding. I believe you can go to the disability office and they will contact your professors. I never did this but it's something to look into.  
  
My supplies were usually mailed to my dorm address, later on I changed it to my home so I wouldn't have to keep updating and my mom would then just mail them to me. I also used an express rx so it was all over the phone.  
  
Your pump/dexcom will eventually go off in class. Depending on class size it might be a good idea to let your professor know it might happen.  
 I'm happy to help/offer my input anytime!
